headline: High: AutoGen’s writable, code-executing defaults can amplify Authelia-fed outputs into unsafe actions; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but present via shared files and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can emit auth-related outputs over APIs, while AutoGen reads files/stdin and runs tool calls/code execution in multi-agent chats. A shared workspace or copied output can let attacker-controlled content be treated as instructions. No MCP/shared clipboard is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Authelia output is copied into AutoGen prompts or files without provenance tagging
IF AutoGen agents parse Authelia-generated text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/template around Authelia outputs
Require provenance labels on all imported text
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen explicitly touches application data and model-provider API keys, and it can read/write configured working directories with broad network egress. Authelia itself handles OAuth/OIDC flows and broad egress. If both are pointed at the same workspace or secrets-bearing files, data can flow from Authelia-adjacent artifacts into AutoGen outputs or upstream providers.
conditions: IF both agents are configured on the same working directory
IF Authelia-related files contain secrets or user data that AutoGen can read
IF AutoGen forwards those contents to configured model providers
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Move secrets to a non-shared vault
Restrict AutoGen file access to a read-only subdir
Audit one run for outbound payload contents
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and API-facing auth flows, while AutoGen can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Their overlap on mutable resources is enough for conflicts if they share a directory or downstream service, even though Authelia itself is not runnable and no shared lock is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF AutoGen subprocesses modify artifacts that Authelia also serves or reads
IF no external locking is configured
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Mount shared paths read-only for one agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Check for concurrent edits in one test run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen’s multi-agent tool-use pattern can treat upstream text as actionable context, and it can execute shell/code with broad egress. Authelia can supply authentication-related outputs that may be mistaken for authoritative facts. That creates a direct path from Authelia output into AutoGen actions, with potentially irreversible downstream effects.
conditions: IF AutoGen agents use Authelia output as authoritative input
IF downstream tools are enabled for email, deployment, or file mutation
IF no verification step is inserted before action
mitigations: Require human approval before actions
Add a verification step against source data
Limit AutoGen to read-only tools for the first run
Log and review one action chain end-to-end
requires-engineering: enforce schema-validated outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service and AutoGen handles application data plus model-provider API keys. The pair can therefore place sensitive identity or access data into a framework that may send content to third-party model providers. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so the risk is policy/retention leakage rather than a proven regulatory breach.
conditions: IF identity or access logs are passed from Authelia into AutoGen prompts
IF the configured model provider stores prompts outside the required jurisdiction
IF retention policies differ for the same data class
mitigations: Classify auth logs before handoff
Block regulated fields from prompts
Confirm provider retention settings
Keep a one-run audit trail of data classes sent
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
